title: The Ninth — Beyond Comprehension
subtitle: Infinite Information & Unknowable Truths

lore.description: Beyond the eighth figure of Sacred Geometry lies a rim no compass will hold. The Ninth is not absence but surplus: knowledge poured past the lip of any vessel, truth that overgrows the frame that seeks to bind it. Those who bend the knee at its lectern become conduits for impossible reckonings — glimpsing patterns that cannot be kept whole inside a single skull. Each revelation purchases power at the price of living comfortably within the world's common measures.
lore.followers: The Ninth does not explain, define, or warn. It overflows. To invoke it is to step past the eighth threshold — the one you did not know was there — and find that on the other side, the cup forgets its shape, the bell rings a note that was never cast, and the answer to your question arrives as a question you had not yet learned to ask. Its followers are scholars, truth-seekers, and those who have looked too long into the void and found it looking back. They are rarely comfortable. They are never entirely sane.

names_across_regions.thepyrgos: The Unfinished Index, the patron of archivists who seek the edges of knowledge
names_across_regions.aeler: The Rim Without Compass, a figure spoken of only in whispers among Truth-Masons
names_across_regions.the_gray_wanderer: The Ninth Cup, the un-poured vessel, the answer that will not fit the question

lore.quote: Eight figures bind the world; the Ninth overflows it. Drink, and remember that the cup forgets its shape before the song is done.

domain_focus: Hyperdimensional Knowledge: reckonings that do not fit a single plane or proof
Incomprehensible Truths: insights that demand the seer be changed to hold them
Information Overflow: boon and peril of minds run past their brim
Conceptual Transcendence: thinking beyond the usual ledgers and names
Threshold Breaking: stepping past the eighth boundary into what should not exist

thiasos.description: The Ninth's Thiasos is an animal touched by impossible patterns: a brass-shelled beetle that walks toward contradictions, a spider whose web changes when someone asks a question, a mirror-scaled minnow that swims through repeated figures, or a white mouse that rearranges scattered counters into sequences no scholar can finish.
thiasos.care: It needs ordinary care and a new piece of information each week: a secret, a riddle, or a half-finished proof. If given nothing new for a month, it becomes Compromised and begins offering persuasive but false answers.

codex.description: No Codex of the Ninth takes the form of a simple grimoire. It may be a slate of fractally etched stone, a bundle of knotted threads, or the inside of the Runekeeper's own eyelids.
codex.upkeep: Because the Ninth's truths resist being fixed in one place, a Codex requires upkeep: the Runekeeper must spend an hour each week erasing and rewriting a single page, or the Rites stored there become garbled (treat as Compromised until restored).

patrons_gift.name: The Overflowing Cup
patrons_gift.description: Once per scene as an action, a Runekeeper of the Ninth may touch a held item (weapon, tool, or writing implement) and speak a paradox.
patrons_gift.effect: For the rest of the scene, the item grants +1 die to Lore or Investigation rolls, and its first use each scene ignores one Story Beat generated by a 1 (the item's impossible nature briefly confuses the Weave).
patrons_gift.cost: After the scene, the user marks +1 Obligation to the Ninth.

rites.name: Rite of the Ninth Figure
rites.materials: A chalk figure with an 'impossible' joint, or a reckoning worked toward infinity on slate.
rites.effect: Glimpse past the ordinary frame of measure. Gain +1 die to Lore or Investigation when wrestling complex systems or many-layered problems.

rites.name: Rite of the Flooded Scriptorium
rites.materials: An overburdened ledger-hall, stacked codices, a bell that tolls the copying-hour without cease.
rites.effect: Read faster than hands can turn pages. Ask three questions upon any topic that leaves a written wake; gain +2 dice to rolls of analysis this scene.
rites.push_it: The tide of knowing overruns its banks — suffer Fatigue 1 and mark 1 SB (Diamonds) as overflow breeds complication. Cost: Mark +1 Obligation (total +2) or Mark +1 Fatigue.

rites.name: Rite of the Hypercognitive Lattice
rites.materials: A brass-thought lattice, an orrery of inked threads, or a draught that sharpens memory.
rites.effect: Widen the mind's mouth. For this scene, treat your Wits as +1 higher for information-processing rolls; you may track several intricate streams at once. Memory Anchor: The insight is overwhelming. You must write a brief summary of what you learned during downtime (a short scene or a full hour of transcription). Without this anchor, the bonus fades at the end of the scene and cannot be recovered.
rites.push_it: The opening does not quite close: keep the boon, but suffer –1 die to single-task focus; mark 1 SB (Clubs). Cost: Mark +1 Obligation (total +2) or Mark +1 Fatigue.

rites.name: Rite of the Breaking Glyph
rites.materials: A vigil in dim light, a water-timer, and a problem sworn not to be left half-seen.
rites.effect: Take one pattern whole. Choose a complex system, theory, or design and gain perfect internal grasp of it; receive +3 dice to related knowledge rolls for the next exchange (one action). The insight is too vast to hold for longer. The GM gains 1 SB as the knowledge strains the mind.
rites.push_it: Your tongue cannot carry what your mind now holds: you cannot clearly teach or translate this insight; mark 1 SB (Hearts). Cost: Mark +1 Obligation (total +2) or Mark +1 Fatigue.

rites.name: Rite of the Endless Stacks
rites.materials: A hall of mirrored shelves, wax-tablets without end, whispering leaves of vellum.
rites.effect: Raise a locus of overfull knowing. All present gain +2 dice to information-work; knowledge may be drawn from unlikely sources. Start a [6] Information Overload timer — as it fills, participants strain and fray.
rites.push_it: The Stacks wake and demand tithe in understanding or memory; mark +2 Obligation. Cost: Mark +1 Obligation (total +3) or Mark +1 Fatigue.

rites.name: Rite of the Ninth Revelation
rites.materials: A fast from easy speech, a circle of unbroken figures, and vows to see past comfort.
rites.effect: Glimpse a shard of Ninth truth. Choose one: perfect command of a knotty system for the next exchange; a single forecast of chaotic motion (one yes/no question answered by the GM); or comprehension of an 'impossible' relation (the GM must answer one question truthfully). You must first succeed on an Investigation or Lore roll against a DV set by the GM (minimum 4). On a failure, the insight is garbled — you gain no benefit, but mark 1 SB (Diamonds) as the knowledge recoils.
rites.push_it: The shard sets in you like glass: gain Transcendent Understanding (see Corruption) and mark +2 Obligation. Cost: Mark +1 Obligation (total +3) or Mark +1 Fatigue.

cantors.name: The Cantor's Song
cantors.description: A Cantor of the Ninth sings in phrases that fold back on themselves — melodies that seem to have no beginning or end, harmonies that shift key in ways that should be impossible. Their voice is used to encrypt a message into a tune that only the intended listener can hear, to unravel the logic of a paradox, or to lull a library's guardian spirit into a momentary confusion. The Ninth's Cantors are often found in great archives, humming while they work.

cult.name: The Cult of the Unfinished Index
cult.description: The Ninth's cults meet in libraries, scriptoria, and the back rooms of printing houses — but the innermost circle, the Unfinished Index, has a stranger practice: each member carves a single extra joint into a finger of their writing hand (a ninth knuckle that does not bend). They believe that the extra joint holds a question they have not yet learned to ask. A ritual involves each member writing a fact they have never told anyone on a slip of paper, then burning it. The ashes are swept into a single book — the Growing Ledger — whose pages multiply each year and whisper at night, adding entries no one wrote. Their creed is stamped inside the cover: 'Every answer births nine new questions. This is not a flaw. This is the shape of truth.' Outsiders are welcome to ask a question, but they will leave with three they did not bring — and sometimes, a faint, extra knuckle that fades by morning.

witchcraft.name: The Art of the Unspoken
witchcraft.description: A witch who walks with the Ninth is a glyph-carver or pattern-weaver — one who crafts knowledge into physical form: a book that writes itself, a map that shows only the routes the reader does not yet know, or a code that cannot be broken because it was never written. Their magic works through the tools of information: a quill that writes in letters that shift meaning with the light, a seal that stamps 'APPROVED' onto documents that were never submitted, or a lens that reveals hidden writing. Their craft is never about forging metal; it is about folding paper, spilling ink, and stepping past the eighth line of a proof into the white space where the answer is not written because the question was wrong.
witchcraft.lore: The glyph-carver learns that some truths cannot be spoken — only unfolded. They do not seek answers; they seek better questions. Their craft is the art of the threshold, and they practice it with every word they do not write.
witchcraft.quote: Eight figures bind the world; the Ninth overflows it.

paradox_quill.name: The Paradox Quill
paradox_quill.description: A quill carved from the bone of a bird that never lived, dipped in ink that dries clear. Once per session, the witch may write a single sentence on a surface (a wall, a scroll, a forehead). The sentence is true — but only for the next hour. After that, it becomes a lie, or fades, or was never there at all. The GM determines the exact effect, but the truth is always useful for that hour.

hedge_gifts.name: Glyph of Unfolding
hedge_gifts.description: Once per scene, the witch may draw a single geometric symbol on a surface (a door, a lock, a piece of paper) while speaking a question aloud. The symbol 'unfolds' into a diagram that answers the question — but the diagram is always incomplete, cryptic, or reveals something the seeker did not wish to know. The witch gains +1 die to any roll that uses the diagram's information.

monastic_tradition.name: Way of the Unfinished Index
monastic_tradition.description: Monks of the Unfinished Index believe that every answer is a door to nine more questions. They do not seek completion—they seek the next page, the next insight, the next threshold. Their minds are open, flexible, and constantly straining against the limits of mortal comprehension. They are never quite satisfied, and they are never quite sane.
monastic_tradition.prerequisites: Wits 3+, Spirit 2+, Rite of the Ninth Figure or Cantor of the Ninth.
monastic_tradition.quote: Every answer births nine new questions. This is not a flaw. This is the shape of truth.
monastic_tradition.debt_resistant_frame: The Ninth does not collect debts—it overflows them. Monks of the Unfinished Index gain +1 die to resist any magical debt, geas, or contract that would limit their access to knowledge or compel them to stop asking questions. If they succeed, the creditor's demand is simply lost in the infinite—the obligation was never recorded in the first place.

basic.name: Hyperawareness
basic.effect: +1 die to Notice when patterns whisper that they matter.

advanced.name: Pattern Recognition
advanced.effect: Once/scene, see connections others miss within tangled accounts and signs.

master.name: Ninth Awareness
master.effect: Once per session, look from outside the frame; for a heartbeat, the world aligns. You may ask the GM one question about a hidden pattern or connection, and they must answer truthfully. After the scene, you gain a permanent Debt Scar (your reflection is slightly wrong, as if seen from an angle that doesn't exist) and you suffer –1 die to all rolls involving easy company for the rest of the session.

monastic_tradition.corruption_note: Monks follow the patron's general Corruption track; the monastic path does not add a second one. Where a tradition needs its own, it must differ from the general track in kind, not degree.

corruption.benefit: Hyperawareness: +1 die to Notice when patterns whisper that they matter.
corruption.cost: Starved for Text: –1 die in barren halls with little record or sign; you itch for a stream to read.

corruption.benefit: Pattern Recognition: Once/scene, see connections others miss within tangled accounts and signs.
corruption.cost: Scattered Threads: Thoughts run in parallel; –1 die to sustained, single-line focus.

corruption.benefit: Data Synthesis: Once/session, fuse vast reckonings at a glance into a usable answer.
corruption.cost: Tongue-Tied by Wonder: –2 dice to teach or clearly explain your deepest insights.

corruption.benefit: Dimensional Insight: Once/scene, take a problem from an 'impossible' angle and treat a knot as if already loosened.
corruption.cost: Bent Sense: Ordinary space and tasks feel ill-fit; –1 die to plain spatial or mundane labors.

corruption.benefit: Infinite Processing: Once/session, render perfect analysis of any information system or record-trail.
corruption.cost: Concept Drift: Common categories slip; –1 die to easy company and familiar talk.

corruption.benefit: Ninth Awareness: Once/session, look from outside the frame; for a heartbeat, the world aligns.
corruption.cost: Transcendent Fragmentation: Mark +3 Obligation. You exist partially out of phase. Once per session, you may phase through a solid obstacle (wall, door, person) as a move action, but after doing so you cannot physically interact with objects for one exchange. The GM gains 1 SB as reality shivers.

playstyle_notes.description: The Ninth favors the patient reader of tangled ledgers and sky-signs alike. It rewards audacity in thought and the courage to let understanding change you. Its gifts turn riddles into roads — but every road leads past a threshold you did not know existed. To serve the Ninth is to accept that you will never again fit comfortably inside the frame you once called home. Intrusions often take the form of sudden, inexplicable knowledge (a face you recognize from a dream, a word in a language you have never learned), or a question posed by a stranger who seems to know exactly what you were thinking. Refusing an intrusion does not bring punishment — merely the slow forgetting of the insight you were about to receive, leaving you with the sense that you once knew something important, but can no longer recall what.
emphasizes: Hyperdimensional Knowledge: insights that escape a single page
Cognitive Expansion: widening the mind to hold more than comfort allows
Pattern Transcendence: seeing threads that run beneath names and weights
Information Synthesis: binding many scraps into one true line
Conceptual Breakthrough: stepping past the frame rather than painting within it
Threshold Overflow: the power of the ninth step, the extra word, the unasked question

sample_adventure.title: The Ninth Cup
sample_adventure.description: In a Thepyrgos archive, a single page has been found that should not exist. It contains a proof of a theorem that contradicts eight known laws of magic. The archivists are afraid to touch it. The Chain-Lanterns want to destroy it. The party is hired to retrieve it — and decide what to do with a truth that cannot be contained. The Ninth is listening. The cup is about to overflow.
sample_adventure.quote: Every answer births nine new questions. This is not a flaw. This is the shape of truth.

_easter_egg_note: The Ninth is a cryptic patron, meant to be discovered through in-game research or whispered rumor. It should not be the first patron a player encounters—it is the one they find when they ask too many questions. Use it sparingly, and never explain it fully. The Ninth is the mystery that never resolves, the truth that always overflows.
names_note: Two names, two registers. **The Ninth** is the general name — the thing behind the Taboo, spoken of by people who have no board in front of them and would rather not be specific. **The Ninth Rim** is the Kon'reh term: the rim beyond the eighth figure, off the edge of a board that only has eight — that board being the Sacred Geometry, which is the Ykrul name for Kon'reh. The Ykrul hold that Kon'reh is not a game about the world but a model of it, so a word for something off the edge of the board is a word for something off the edge of everything. To a Ykrul the two names are the same statement made at different volumes; to anyone else, the Kon'reh term is the one that sounds like it means less, which is why it survives in places the other cannot be said aloud.

guises.name: The Unfinished Index
guises.note: A copying desk is sometimes left with its work facedown after its keeper retires. Successors find the material useful until a reference points to a shelf the room has never contained. Some reconstruct the absent shelf. Others catalog the reference without following it. Neither practice has reliably prevented further entries from appearing.

guises.name: The Rim Without Compass
guises.note: A measured figure is shown with the place where its boundary ceased to agree with the instrument. Apprentices are asked to reproduce the known part before hearing the account. In severe Himadri schools the flawed tracing may remain under a cover; Qianvar workshops sometimes display it beside the tools. Neither can turn its method of custody into proof that the next tracing will remain contained.

guises.name: The Citation Without a Place
guises.note: A correspondent answers an ordinary question with an observation the recipient can verify and no one recalls sending. The pavilions' keepers may help identify the manuscript from which part of it came. Their refusal to supply a final explanation is not evidence that they possess one. An official who orders a complete account may receive considerably more writing than the order required.

guises.name: The Ninth Cup
guises.note: The cup remains unpoured while people decide where the next night's shelter will be. Those who seek the surplus bring a question they have rehearsed alone. Sometimes they leave with an answer and no longer recognize the problem that made them ask. The host still packs food for the journey and avoids counting the vessels aloud.

provenance.origin: There is no secure foundation date for a practice whose surviving accounts keep acquiring material outside their own scope.
provenance.summary: The Unfinished Index can identify gatherings, copied sheets, and teachers. It cannot establish a first revelation from the age of a page. A later hand can copy an older observation; a perfectly authenticated early volume can refer to work not yet written. The uncertainty has encouraged counterfeit discoveries as well as genuine encounters. Identifying a forgery does not settle what is happening in another book.
provenance.the_migration: Correspondence carried the practice without requiring a missionary. A useful result attracted a second question, and readers formed circles to compare what they had received. Printers sometimes duplicated an extra line that no editor had accepted. Manuscript keepers accused the presses; presses pointed to older copies carrying the same addition. The disagreement moved through trade routes faster than the custodians could compare their evidence.
provenance.why_it_took: Some revelations have saved lives or resolved problems that defeated years of work. This is why experienced readers return. The danger is not disproved by a correct answer. A scholar may cease sleeping while remaining courteous, useful, and unable to stop explaining a conclusion whose beginning everybody else has forgotten. The company keeps asking because the next part appears to concern them personally.
provenance.note: Regional ninth taboos are not declarations of membership in this cult. A household that stops at eight may never invoke the Patron catalogued here. Cult histories record encounters with surplus knowledge; they do not reveal the ultimate explanation of the world's taboos.

philosophy.name: An Answer Larger Than Its Keeper
philosophy.summary: Understanding something can alter the conditions under which the understanding is held. The reader who began the investigation may not be able to remain its unchanged custodian.
philosophy.the_point: Institutions often ask whether an observation is true before deciding whether it should circulate. The Ninth makes a second question unavoidable: what happens to a person who can no longer stop receiving the rest of it?
philosophy.the_third_thing: An incomplete account can be an honest account. Some keepers leave the break visible rather than filling it with an invented conclusion. The empty space may remain empty. The next person through the room should not be required to test it.
philosophy.at_the_table: Choose a useful, limited revelation and particular observable disturbances. Do not present a cosmological lecture, a universal decoding of ninth taboos, or a single mandatory response. Closing the book, restricting circulation, and seeking help must remain actions characters can attempt without being mocked for refusing more.
